symbols.name: \delta_0
symbols.role: Certified common radius for original-coordinate conic neighborhoods and Whitney extension.

symbols.name: P^{\mathrm{fs}}
symbols.space: Laws of fixed-\(T\) panel observations with a finite mover support.
symbols.role: Separate finite-support comparison law, not a member of the absolutely continuous class \(\mathcal P_\Sigma\).

symbols.name: S
symbols.role: Fixed mover support recorded in the geometry signature.

symbols.name: \mathbf g
symbols.def: \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:g_b(x)\ge0,\ 1\le b\le J_0\}\), with irredundant sign conditions recording every active support face.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M(x)_{i,k+1}=x_{K+i-k}\) for \(1\le i\le r\) and \(0\le k\le K\).

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.role: Orthogonal projector onto the complement of the column space.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{\rm rk}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_{\rm rk}=\langle\det M_I: I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\},\ |I|=p\rangle\), where \(M_I\) is the \(p\times p\) row submatrix of \(M\).

symbols.name: H_k
symbols.def: \(H_k(x)=\|(M(x)')^+e_k\|_2\) for every \(x\), using the Moore--Penrose inverse; in particular \(H_k(0)=0\).

symbols.name: \overline H_{\Sigma,k}
symbols.role: Signature-specific global leverage ceiling; it is finite exactly in the bounded-score branch derived by the tail-atlas theorem.

symbols.name: \widetilde\mu_k
symbols.role: A representative extending \(\mu_k\) with \(C^{s-1,1}\) regularity in the original treatment-history coordinates.

symbols.name: \Sigma
symbols.def: \(\Sigma=(T,K,S,\mathbf g,\mathcal I_{\rm rk},(A_0,\ldots,A_K),\mathfrak S,\text{normal-link certificate record})\), where \(\mathfrak S\) is the canonical original-coordinate stratification by rank depth, alignment, and active support faces, and all entries have rational or real-algebraic codes.
symbols.role: Support, rank-ideal, alignment, face, and normal-link data held fixed across a minimax class.

symbols.name: \mathscr A_\Sigma
symbols.type: Finite certified resolution atlas with partition of unity.
symbols.role: One frozen atlas used only for Hölder norms and implementation.

symbols.name: j
symbols.type: Index of a chart in \(\mathscr A_\Sigma\).

symbols.name: \omega_j
symbols.def: \((\omega_j)_j\) is the deterministic partition of unity subordinate to \(\mathscr A_\Sigma\), ordered by the certificate's canonical semialgebraic code.

symbols.name: \mathbf b_j
symbols.role: Chart valuation of the Jacobian and active boundary orthant.

symbols.name: Z_k(z)
symbols.type: Extended-real local-zeta integral indexed by real \(z\).
symbols.role: Mellin integral whose first positive singularity determines the leverage-tail index.

symbols.name: Z_{k,s}(z)
symbols.type: Extended-real distance-weighted local-zeta integral indexed by real \(z\).
symbols.role: Mellin integral whose first positive singularity determines the frontier-remainder index.

symbols.name: \zeta_{\Sigma,k,s}
symbols.role: Resolution-invariant power of the frontier remainder.

symbols.name: \ell_{\Sigma,k,s}
symbols.role: Resolution-invariant logarithmic multiplicity of the frontier remainder.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,C}
symbols.role: Order-\(s-1\) Taylor extension defined by the frozen atlas.

symbols.name: A_C
symbols.role: Closed finite-leverage anchor set for cutoff \(C\).

symbols.name: A_{jC}
symbols.role: Part of \(A_C\) meeting the support of partition weight \(\omega_j\).

symbols.name: p_C
symbols.role: Canonical Euclidean projection onto \(A_C\) when that set is nonempty.

symbols.name: p_{jC}
symbols.role: Canonical chart-anchor selector with fallback to \(p_C\).

symbols.name: x_\Sigma
symbols.role: Fixed signature-coded value used only to totalize empty-anchor cases.

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{\Sigma,k,s}
symbols.role: Selector-distance integral controlling Taylor extrapolation error.

symbols.name: \overline V_{\Sigma,k}
symbols.role: Worst-case truncated variance over the fixed-signature class.

symbols.name: \mathcal G_{G,\Sigma}
symbols.role: Tie-broken geometric cutoff grid with an infinity option.

symbols.name: \operatorname{Risk}_{G,k}(\Sigma)
symbols.role: Exact minimax squared risk over the fixed-signature class.

symbols.name: \operatorname{Len}_{G,k}(\Sigma,\eta)
symbols.role: Exact shortest uniformly honest worst-case expected length.

assumptions.condition: \((W_g)_{g=1}^G\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P\).

standard.name: Conditional mean independence of differenced disturbances
Positive stayer mass bounded away from one

assumptions.condition: \(\underline f\le f_X(x)\le\overline f\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in S\).
The mover support, its irredundant defining inequalities, and its active face incidences are exactly the \(S\), \(\mathbf g\), and face data recorded by the fixed signature \(\Sigma\).

novel.justification: A treatment design fixes dose bounds and admissible reversal histories before outcomes are sampled. Boxes and polytopes used for bounded continuous doses therefore define natural fixed-signature subclasses instead of a resolution-dependent union of laws.

assumptions.condition: The original-coordinate certificate \(\mathfrak C_\Sigma\) supplies semialgebraic conic bi-Lipschitz parametrizations with strict algebraically checkable angle and transverse-Jacobian bounds, together with certified lower and upper link-mass intervals, for every active rank-depth, target-alignment, and support-face stratum of \(\Sigma\).

novel.justification: The certificate records quantitative local conic regularity of a fixed treatment-history region, not a desired probability exponent. Dose boxes and polytopes used in reversible-treatment panels have explicit face cones, while an effective semialgebraic volume-bounding algorithm verifies the strict link-mass intervals without treating numerical volume inequalities as first-order polynomial formulas.

standard.name: Uniform higher-moment envelope for random coefficients and disturbances

assumptions.condition: \(\underline\sigma^2 I_r\preceq E_P[\varepsilon\varepsilon'\mid X=x]\preceq\overline\sigma^2 I_r\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in S\).

standard.name: Uniform conditional variance nondegeneracy and boundedness

assumptions.condition: The mover-a.e. function \(\mu_k\) has a representative admitting an original-coordinate Whitney extension \(\widetilde\mu_k\in C^{s-1,1}(N_{\delta_0}(S))\) with \(\|\widetilde\mu_k\|_{C^{s-1,1}}\le L_s\).

novel.justification: This is a primitive smoothness condition on the conditional mean in the observed treatment-history coordinates. It is satisfied by bounded linear, polynomial, and smooth saturation response surfaces on a neighborhood of a dose box or polytope; Sasaki and Ura's scalar derivative correction motivates the order of correction but does not supply this multivariate condition.

definitions.name: \mathfrak C_\Sigma
definitions.construction: For each original-coordinate stratum \(R\in\mathfrak S\), form its base-space normal link \(L_R(x,t)=\{v\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:x+tv\in S,\ t/2\le\operatorname{dist}(x+tv,R)\le t\}\), refined by rank depth, target activity, and support-face signs. The finite certificate gives a semialgebraic conic bi-Lipschitz parametrization of every nonempty sector and explicit \(\delta_0,c_L,C_L,c_\angle,C_\angle,c_J,C_J>0\). Polynomial identities and interval bounds certify the angle, Lipschitz, and transverse normal-Jacobian inequalities on \(0<t\le\delta_0\); an effective cylindrical-decomposition integration algorithm returns rational intervals contained in \([c_L,C_L]\) for the required Hausdorff link masses. The record contains no chart label and no asserted tail power.

definitions.name: \mathscr A_\Sigma
definitions.construction: Choose the lexicographically first normalized boundary-compatible principalization certified from \(\Sigma\). It principalizes the maximal-minor ideal \(\mathcal I_{\rm rk}\), every alignment polynomial \(A_k\), every active support-face ideal and inequality, and the semialgebraic graph of \(x\mapsto\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal Z)\). On chart \(j\), \(Q\circ\phi_j=u_{Qj}\prod_a|z_a|^{q_{ja}}\), \(A_k\circ\phi_j=u_{Akj}\prod_a|z_a|^{a_{kja}}\), \(\operatorname{dist}(\phi_j(z),\mathcal Z)=u_{Dj}\prod_a|z_a|^{d_{ja}}\), and \(|\det D\phi_j|=u_{Jj}\prod_a|z_a|^{b_{ja}}\), with certified unit bounds on the assigned orthant. Fix a smooth subordinate partition of unity \((\omega_j)_j\), refine it into disjoint canonical semialgebraic chart cells by assigning a point to the least coded chart whose cutoff is positive, and record cutoff vanishing orders on every incident face. The atlas is frozen only for evaluating the indices and implementing extrapolation; smoothness is imposed in the original coordinates.

definitions.name: \mathcal P_\Sigma(T,K,s,q,\mathbf c)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_\Sigma(T,K,s,q,\mathbf c)=\{P:\text{ass:at-least-square, ass:iid-groups, ass:distributed-lag-model, ass:conditional-mean-zero, ass:stayer-mass, ass:mover-density, ass:density-envelope, ass:fixed-signature-support, ass:normal-link-certificate, ass:q-moments, ass:noise-variance, and ass:frontier-holder hold for the fixed }\Sigma\}\).

definitions.name: (\alpha_{\Sigma,k},m_{\Sigma,k},\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s},\ell_{\Sigma,k,s})
definitions.construction: Define \(Z_k(z)=\int_{S\cap\{Q>0,H_k>1\}}H_k(x)^z\,dx\) and \(Z_{k,s}(z)=\int_{S\cap\{Q>0,H_k>1\}}H_k(x)^z\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal Z)^s\,dx\). If \(H_k\) is unbounded on \(S\cap\{Q>0\}\), let \(\alpha_{\Sigma,k}\) and \(\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s}\) be their abscissae of convergence, equivalently their first positive real poles after certified semialgebraic resolution, and set \(m_{\Sigma,k}=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha_{\Sigma,k}}Z_k-1\) and \(\ell_{\Sigma,k,s}=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s}}Z_{k,s}-1\). Equivalently, on each realizable simultaneous-zero face of a disjoint canonical chart cell set \(c_{kja}=(q_{ja}-a_{kja})/2>0\): minimize \((b_{ja}+1)/c_{kja}\), or \((b_{ja}+1+s d_{ja})/c_{kja}\), over incident coordinates. The pole order is the maximum number of minimizing coordinates tied within one germ; positive contributions tied across distinct chart cells add residues without increasing that order. Recorded cutoff valuations remove faces on which the partition weight vanishes. If \(H_k\) is bounded, set \((\alpha_{\Sigma,k},m_{\Sigma,k},\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s},\ell_{\Sigma,k,s})=(\infty,0,\infty,0)\).

definitions.name: (A_C,A_{jC},p_C,p_{jC},x_\Sigma)
definitions.construction: For finite \(C\), let \(A_C=\overline{S\cap\{Q>0,H_k\le C\}}\) and \(A_{jC}=A_C\cap\operatorname{supp}\omega_j\). Fix the lexicographically least signature-coded point \(x_\Sigma\in S\). If \(A_C\ne\varnothing\), let \(p_C(x)\) be the lexicographically least point among the Euclidean minimizers of \(y\mapsto\|x-y\|_2\) over \(A_C\), and let \(p_{jC}(x)\) be the analogous selector over \(A_{jC}\), falling back to \(p_C(x)\) when \(A_{jC}=\varnothing\). If \(A_C=\varnothing\), set \(p_C(x)=p_{jC}(x)=x_\Sigma\).

definitions.name: (\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s},\mathcal D_{\Sigma,k,s})
definitions.construction: For finite \(C\), define \(\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)=\int_{S\cap\{Q>0,H_k>C\}}\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal Z)^s\,dx\) and \(\mathcal D_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)=\sum_j\int_{S\cap\{Q>0,H_k>C\}}\omega_j(x)\|x-p_{jC}(x)\|_2^s\,dx\) whenever \(A_C\ne\varnothing\). Set both functions to zero at \(C=\infty\), and set \(\mathcal D_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)=0\) when \(A_C=\varnothing\), the corresponding cutoff being excluded from the effective oracle grid. Both are original-coordinate integrals; the disjoint canonical cell refinement evaluates \(\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s}\) without overlap multiplicity.

definitions.name: \mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,C}
definitions.construction: For finite \(C\) with \(A_C\ne\varnothing\), define \((\mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,C}\mu_k)(x)=\mu_k(x)\) when \(H_k(x)\le C\), and otherwise define it as \(\sum_j\omega_j(x)\sum_{|\beta|\le s-1}D^\beta\widetilde\mu_k(p_{jC}(x))(x-p_{jC}(x))^\beta/\beta!\). If \(A_C=\varnothing\), set \(\mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,C}\mu_k=0\). Set \(\mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,\infty}\mu_k=\mu_k\).

definitions.name: (V_{P,k},\overline V_{\Sigma,k},\overline{\mathfrak B}_{\Sigma,k,s})
definitions.construction: Define \(V_{P,k}(C)=E_P[(e_k'M(X)^+(\Delta Y-\Gamma)-\tau_k)^2\mathbf 1\{H_k(X)\le C\}\mid X\ne0]\), \(\overline V_{\Sigma,k}(C)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma}V_{P,k}(C)\), and \(\overline{\mathfrak B}_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma}|E_P[\mathbf 1\{H_k(X)>C\}\{(\mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,C}\mu_k)(X)-\mu_k(X)\}\mid X\ne0]|\). At \(C=\infty\), the bias is zero and the variance may be infinite.

definitions.name: (\mathcal G_{G,\Sigma},C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star},R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star})
definitions.construction: Fix numerical \(a_0>1\) and the signature-coded degree cap \(\kappa_\Sigma>0\). Let \(\mathcal G_{G,\Sigma}=\{a_0^m:0\le m\le\lceil\kappa_\Sigma\log(G+1)\rceil,\ A_{a_0^m}\ne\varnothing\}\cup\{\infty\}\). Every omitted finite cutoff is still assigned the total zero extension for diagnostic evaluation but is not oracle-eligible. Define \(C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\) as the least finite minimizer, with \(\infty\) ordered last, of \(G^{-1}\overline V_{\Sigma,k}(C)+\overline{\mathfrak B}_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)^2\), using \(+\infty\) when \(\overline V_{\Sigma,k}(C)=\infty\). The grid is finite and nonempty because it contains \(\infty\). Define \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}=G^{-1}\overline V_{\Sigma,k}(C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star})+\overline{\mathfrak B}_{\Sigma,k,s}(C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star})^2\).

definitions.name: (\operatorname{Risk}_{G,k}(\Sigma),\operatorname{Len}_{G,k}(\Sigma,\eta))
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Risk}_{G,k}(\Sigma)=\inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma}E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_k(P))^2]\). Also \(\operatorname{Len}_{G,k}(\Sigma,\eta)=\inf_{\mathcal C:\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma}P\{\tau_k(P)\in\mathcal C\}\ge1-\eta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma}E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)]\), where the infima range over all measurable, possibly randomized procedures based on \(W_1,\ldots,W_G\).

definitions.name: \widehat\Gamma
definitions.construction: On a training fold \(I^c\), let \(\widehat P_{I^c}=|I^c|^{-1}\sum_{g\in I^c}\Pi(M(X_g))\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat P_{I^c})\ge\underline\pi/2\), set \(\widehat\Gamma_{I^c}=\widehat P_{I^c}^{-1}|I^c|^{-1}\sum_{g\in I^c}\Pi(M(X_g))\Delta Y_g\); otherwise set it to the translation-equivariant fold mean \(|I^c|^{-1}\sum_{g\in I^c}\Delta Y_g\). A fold with no observations returns the zero vector.

definitions.name: \widehat\tau_k(C)
definitions.construction: Use a fixed positive number of deterministic folds and the frozen partition. For a validation mover set \(Z_{gk}=e_k'M(X_g)^+(\Delta Y_g-\widehat\Gamma_{I^c})\), and set \(Z_{gk}=0\) when \(X_g=0\). Let \(v_s(u)=(u^\beta)_{|\beta|\le s-1}\), \(K_d(u)=c_d\prod_{a=1}^d(1-u_a^2)_+\), and, for finite \(C\), \(h_{G,C,\Sigma}=\min\{\delta_0/8,[(1+C^2)\log(G+1)/G]^{1/(2s+d)}\}\). At each query \(x\) and chart \(j\), put \(a=p_{jC}(x)\), \(u_g=(X_g-a)/h_{G,C,\Sigma}\), and \(w_{gjC}(a)=\mathbf 1\{g\in I^c,X_g\ne0,H_k(X_g)\le C\}\omega_j(X_g)K_d(u_g)\). Define \[\widehat\theta_{kjC}(a)=\left\{\sum_gw_{gjC}(a)v_s(u_g)v_s(u_g)'+G^{-2}I\right\}^{-1}\sum_gw_{gjC}(a)v_s(u_g)Z_{gk}.\] The ridge makes every normal equation total; if the weighted cell is empty its right-hand side and coefficient vector are zero. Put \(\widehat m_{kj,C}(x)=v_s((x-a)/h_{G,C,\Sigma})'\widehat\theta_{kjC}(a)\). If \(A_C=\varnothing\), set every finite-cutoff fitted extension to zero. Average \(\mathbf 1\{H_k(X_g)\le C\}Z_{gk}+\mathbf 1\{H_k(X_g)>C\}\sum_j\omega_j(X_g)\widehat m_{kj,C}(X_g)\) over validation movers and folds, returning zero if every validation fold has no mover. For \(C=\infty\), omit fitting and average the globally defined Moore--Penrose scores. This defines zero movers, empty cells, singular polynomial Gram matrices, singular history matrices, and every cutoff event.

definitions.name: \widehat C_k
definitions.construction: Across \(\mathcal G_{G,\Sigma}\), use treatment-history-only empirical exceedance counts, all frozen-atlas cell occupancies, and cross-fitted chartwise remainder comparisons in a Goldenshluger--Lepski selector. The selector receives \(\Sigma\) and \(\mathbf c\), but receives neither \(\Gamma\), \(\mu_k\), a dominating active stratum, nor any tail or bias index. Stack the selected lag scores with the total projector estimator and calibrate bias-aware marginal or simultaneous intervals; deterministic ordering resolves every tie and the infinity option is always admissible.

statements.statement: For every full-column-rank history \(x\), \[H_k(x)^2=e_k'(M(x)'M(x))^{-1}e_k=\frac{A_k(x)}{Q(x)}.\] At a smooth rank-\((p-1)\) point \(x_0\in\mathcal Z\) with unit right-kernel vector \(v_0\), target activity \(e_k'v_0\ne0\) implies \(H_k(x)\asymp |e_k'v_0|/\sigma_p(M(x))\) on a sufficiently small conic neighborhood. On any incident exceptional divisor for which the valuation of \(A_k\) is at least that of \(Q\), the globally defined \(H_k\) remains locally bounded; this is target-inactive cancellation.
statements.justification: The identity isolates the exact numerator--denominator geometry for one lag and keeps target-inactive rank loss out of the irregular frontier.
statements.gap: deChaisemartinDHa2025 gives the coordinate Moore--Penrose score and ConcaEtAl2018 gives the rank skeleton, but neither gives a divisorial coordinate-cancellation criterion.
statements.consumer: The result is the algebraic input for the signature and prevents needless trimming of a lag whose target alignment cancels rank loss.

statements.statement: Validity of \(\mathfrak C_\Sigma\) is decidable from the real-algebraic codes for \(\mathbf g\), the generators of \(\mathcal I_{\rm rk}\), and \((A_0,\ldots,A_K)\). Quantifier elimination verifies the conic parametrization identities and strict angle, bi-Lipschitz, and Jacobian inequalities; an effective cylindrical-decomposition integration algorithm encloses each semialgebraic Hausdorff link mass in rational intervals until it either verifies the certificate's strict lower and upper bounds or returns a violating cell. Every compact full-dimensional rational box or rational polytope \(S\) with nonempty full-rank interior admits such a finite certificate after the canonical rank, alignment, face, and Whitney refinement. The certificate permits boundary tangencies and corners by recording their refined normal links rather than imposing global transversality.
statements.justification: A fixed minimax class needs a checkable geometric envelope in the original treatment-history coordinates rather than constants chosen after a resolution is seen.
statements.gap: Wongkew1993 gives global upper tube bounds, while PhongSturm2000 gives algebraic stratification; neither supplies a decidable two-sided normal-link certificate for a support with target alignment and active faces.
statements.consumer: Designers can certify a declared dose box or polytope before estimation and obtain explicit constants for the tail and fitting theorems.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma(T,K,s,q,\mathbf c)\), \(E_P[\Pi(M(X))]\succeq\underline\pi I_r\). On every training fold the fallback event in the total estimator satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma}P\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat P_{I^c})<\underline\pi/2\}\le 2r\exp(-c_\pi|I^c|)\) for a fixed \(c_\pi>0\). The cross-fitted \(\widehat\Gamma\) is uniformly \(G^{-1/2}\)-consistent and asymptotically linear, and the fallback contribution to every oracle lag estimator is \(o(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star 1/2})\).
statements.justification: The common trend remains a regular nuisance, but a total procedure must control the exact event on which its empirical projector equation is singular.
statements.gap: deChaisemartinDHa2025 identifies the regular time-invariant trend but does not propagate a thresholded projector inverse and its translation-equivariant fallback through geometry trimming.
statements.consumer: The result permits one stable common-trend fit for every lag in \(\texttt{dist\_lag\_het}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(A=E_P[\Pi(M(X))]\). Since \(M(0)=0\), the Moore--Penrose inverse of \(M(0)\) is zero and \(\Pi(M(0))=I_r\). Every orthogonal projector is positive semidefinite. Therefore, using the stayer-mass assumption,
\[
A=\pi_0 I_r+E_P[\Pi(M(X))\mathbf 1\{X\ne0\}]
\succeq \pi_0I_r\succeq\underline\pi I_r.
\]

On a training fold of size \(n\), put \(A_n=n^{-1}\sum_{g=1}^n\Pi(M(X_g))\). For a fixed unit vector \(v\), the summands \(v'\Pi(M(X_g))v\) lie in \([0,1]\). A \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere has at most \(9^r\) elements, and the elementary net inequality for symmetric matrices gives
\[
\|A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le 2\max_{v\in\mathcal N}|v'(A_n-A)v|.
\]
Hoeffding's exponential-moment argument for bounded scalar summands and a union bound thus give
\[
P\{\lambda_{\min}(A_n)<\underline\pi/2\}
\le P\{\|A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\underline\pi/2\}
\le 2\,9^r\exp(-n\underline\pi^2/32).
\]
Because \(r\) and \(\underline\pi\) are fixed, decreasing the exponent constant handles the finitely many smaller \(n\) and yields \(2r\exp(-c_\pi n)\) for some \(c_\pi>0\).

On the complementary event, the distributed-lag equation, \(\Pi(M)M=0\), and conditional mean zero imply the exact identity
\[
\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma
=A_n^{-1}\frac1n\sum_{g=1}^n\Pi(M(X_g))\varepsilon_g.
\]
The compactness of \(S\), the \(q\)-moment assumption, and \(q>4\) give uniform second and fourth moments for the summand. Also \(\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\underline\pi^{-1}\), \(A_n-A=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and the resolvent identity gives
\[
A_n^{-1}-A^{-1}=A^{-1}(A-A_n)A_n^{-1}=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Consequently
\[
\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma
=A^{-1}\frac1n\sum_{g=1}^n\Pi(M(X_g))\varepsilon_g+O_P(n^{-1}),
\]
uniformly over the fixed-signature class. This is the asserted uniform root-\(G\) consistency and asymptotic linearity because the number of folds is fixed and every nonempty fold has size proportional to \(G\).

On the fallback event, translation equivariance gives
\[
\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma
=\frac1n\sum_{g=1}^n\{M(X_g)B_g+\varepsilon_g\}.
\]
The compact support of \(X\) and the \(q\)-moment envelope bound its \(q\)-th moment by a fixed polynomial in \(n\). Every finite grid cutoff is at most polynomial in \(G\). Hölder's inequality combined with the exponential fallback probability therefore makes its contribution to every trimmed oracle score smaller than every inverse power of \(G\). When \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}>0\), the finite semialgebraic grid and the tail atlas make \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star 1/2}\) at worst polynomially small. If \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}=0\), the noise-variance lower bound forces the selected truncated score to vanish almost surely, while the zero uniform bias forces the corresponding fitted oracle summand to vanish; the fallback contribution is then identically zero. In both cases it is \(o(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star 1/2})\).

statements.statement: Fix a certified signature \(\Sigma\). The local-zeta abscissae and pole orders in \(Z_k(z)\) and \(Z_{k,s}(z)\) equal the simultaneous-face rule in \(\text{def:invariant-indices}\), and every normalized boundary-compatible resolution subordinate to the rank ideal, alignment polynomials, support faces, distance graph, and canonical cutoff cells yields the same pairs \((\alpha_{\Sigma,k},m_{\Sigma,k})\) and \((\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s},\ell_{\Sigma,k,s})\). Exactly one of two branches holds. In the unbounded branch, both powers are finite and, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma(T,K,s,q,\mathbf c)\), for all sufficiently large finite \(u\) and \(C\), \[P\{H_k(X)>u\mid X\ne0\}\asymp u^{-\alpha_{\Sigma,k}}(\log u)^{m_{\Sigma,k}},\qquad\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)\asymp C^{-\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s}}(\log C)^{\ell_{\Sigma,k,s}}.\] In the bounded-score branch, \((\alpha_{\Sigma,k},m_{\Sigma,k},\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s},\ell_{\Sigma,k,s})=(\infty,0,\infty,0)\), \(\overline H_{\Sigma,k}<\infty\), and both displayed tails are zero above that ceiling. The constants depend only on \(\Sigma\) and \(\mathbf c\). Divisors with nonpositive leverage valuation are target inactive. The conclusion includes active support faces, tangencies, higher-rank intersections, ties within a germ, and additive ties across chart cells; vanishing partition weights cannot alter a pole order.
statements.justification: This is the geometric kernel: fixed original-coordinate data, rather than a chosen resolution or an assumed tube power, determine each lag's complete tail and bias indices.
statements.gap: ConcaEtAl2018 identifies Hankel rank ideals, PhongSturm2000 supplies a local-zeta framework, and Wongkew1993 supplies upper tubes; none proves resolution-invariant two-sided laws for this boundary-weighted coordinate ratio.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies the cutoff geometry and leverage diagnostic for continuous-treatment \(\texttt{dist\_lag\_het}\).

statements.statement: Let \(K=1\), \(T=5\), \(x^\star=(1,-1,1,-1)\), and let the mover density be constant on \(U_\rho=x^\star+[-\rho,\rho]^4\) for sufficiently small \(\rho>0\). For \(M(x)=((x_2,x_1),(x_3,x_2),(x_4,x_3))'\), the Jacobian of the three maximal minors has rank two at \(x^\star\), the right kernel is spanned by \((1,1)'\), and for both \(k=0,1\), \[u^2P\{H_k(X)>u\mid X\in U_\rho\}\longrightarrow C_{k,\rho}\in(0,\infty).\] For \(K=1,T=4\), \(H_0=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}/|x_2^2-x_1x_3|\) and \(H_1=\sqrt{x_2^2+x_3^2}/|x_2^2-x_1x_3|\), giving the smooth target-active pair \((\alpha_{\Sigma,k},m_{\Sigma,k})=(1,0)\).
statements.justification: The alternating-history limit is the prespecified early-kill test for the codimension-two critical frontier and both target coordinates.
statements.gap: Neither deChaisemartinDHa2025 nor the Hankel determinantal literature computes this local probability-tail constant.
statements.consumer: The proposition is a numerical and symbolic unit test for any certified-atlas implementation.

statements.statement: For every finite cutoff with \(A_C\ne\varnothing\), the lexicographically tie-broken Euclidean argmin maps \(p_C\) and \(p_{jC}\) are Borel measurable jointly in \((x,C)\). Uniformly over the effective grid, \[\mathcal D_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)=\sum_j\int_{S\cap\{Q>0,H_k>C\}}\omega_j(x)\|x-p_{jC}(x)\|_2^s\,dx\le C_{\Sigma,s}\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s}(C).\] Consequently the explicit partition-of-unity Taylor extension satisfies \(\int_{H_k>C}|(\mathcal E_{\Sigma,k,s,C}\mu_k)(x)-\mu_k(x)|\,dx\le C_{\Sigma,s}L_s\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)\). The conclusion includes chart overlaps and empty \(A_{jC}\) through the prescribed fallback.
statements.justification: The Taylor correction is well posed only when its cross-chart anchors are measurable and their displacement has the same order as the distance-weighted frontier integral.
statements.gap: SasakiUra2022 uses one scalar boundary, whereas no cited result controls canonical Euclidean anchor selectors across intersecting Hankel and support-face strata.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the deterministic bias bound used by the oracle estimator without hiding chart selection inside an informal fitting step.

statements.statement: For every cutoff \(C\in\mathcal G_{G,\Sigma}\), the displayed ridge normal equations, anchor maps, fold scores, and partition sum define a jointly measurable total estimator. It uses neither \(\Gamma\), \(\mu_k\), a dominating stratum, nor the four resolution indices as inputs. Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_\Sigma\), its stochastic local-polynomial fitting error plus the generated-\(\Gamma\) error is bounded at \(C=C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\) by a constant multiple of \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star 1/2}\), and \[\overline{\mathfrak B}_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)\le C_{\Sigma,s}L_s\mathcal D_{\Sigma,k,s}(C)\le C'_{\Sigma,s}L_s\mathcal J_{\Sigma,k,s}(C).\] Empty weighted cells, ridge regularization, singular local designs, and projector fallback events contribute no larger order uniformly.
statements.justification: The geometric oracle rate is meaningful only if estimating the chartwise extrapolation and common trend does not silently dominate its deterministic bias--variance balance.
statements.gap: SasakiUra2022 controls a scalar corrected ratio, but it has no intersecting Hankel cells, frozen partition, or generated regular projector nuisance.
statements.consumer: This lemma turns the class-level oracle criterion into an implementable upper-bound estimator for a fixed certified signature.

statements.statement: For each fixed certified \(\Sigma\), there is \(C<\infty\), depending only on \(\Sigma,\mathbf c,s,q,\eta\), such that for all large \(G\), \[\operatorname{Risk}_{G,k}(\Sigma)\le C R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star},\qquad\operatorname{Len}_{G,k}(\Sigma,\eta)\le C\sqrt{R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}}.\] The upper risk is attained by \(\widehat\tau_k(C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star})\), and a bias-aware interval using the uniform bias envelope attains the length bound. For \(0<\alpha_{\Sigma,k}<2\), write \(v_{\Sigma,k}=2-\alpha_{\Sigma,k}\). The oracle upper-bound scale is \[R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\asymp\begin{cases}G^{-1},&2<\alpha_{\Sigma,k}\le\infty,\\G^{-1}(\log G)^{m_{\Sigma,k}+1},&\alpha_{\Sigma,k}=2,\\G^{-2\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s}/(v_{\Sigma,k}+2\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s})}(\log G)^{2\{\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s}m_{\Sigma,k}+\ell_{\Sigma,k,s}v_{\Sigma,k}\}/(v_{\Sigma,k}+2\zeta_{\Sigma,k,s})},&0<\alpha_{\Sigma,k}<2.\end{cases}\] The equality case \(\alpha_{\Sigma,k}=2\), every logarithmic multiplicity, and the bounded-score branch are retained. No tail or bias index, active stratum, \(\Gamma\), or \(\mu_k\) is supplied to the estimator.
statements.justification: The tail atlas has econometric content only if it yields a total estimator and uniformly honest interval at the class-level oracle frontier.
statements.gap: GrahamPowell2012 provides a scalar trimmed limit law and SasakiUra2022 provides scalar bias correction; neither gives a fixed-signature multivariate Hankel oracle upper bound with exact pole multiplicities.
statements.consumer: Applied users receive a lagwise upper-bound rule for regular, critical, and irregular reporting under a declared treatment-history geometry.

statements.statement: The construction has three literal reductions. First, let \(P^{\mathrm{fs}}\) be a separate law with independent groups, the distributed-lag equation and conditional-mean-zero restriction, positive stayer mass, bounded moments, and finitely many eligible mover histories, every one separated from \(\mathcal Z\). This discrete law is not an element of the absolutely continuous class \(\mathcal P_\Sigma\). Under \(P^{\mathrm{fs}}\), \(H_k\) is bounded on the mover support, the untrimmed Moore--Penrose score identifies \(\tau_k(P^{\mathrm{fs}})\), and the tuning-free finite-support estimator of deChaisemartinDHa2025 has squared risk of order \(G^{-1}\) and Wald expected length of order \(G^{-1/2}\) under nondegenerate score variance. Second, inside the continuous scalar class with \(K=0\), \(T=2\), mover density positive at zero, and \(H_0(x)\asymp|x|^{-1}\), \[\mathcal J_{\Sigma,0,s}(C)\asymp\mathcal D_{\Sigma,0,s}(C)\asymp\int_{|x|<c/C}|x|^s\,dx\asymp C^{-(s+1)}.\] Hence \((\alpha_{\Sigma,0},m_{\Sigma,0},\zeta_{\Sigma,0,1},\ell_{\Sigma,0,1})=(1,0,2,0)\), \(C_{G,\Sigma,0}^{\star}\asymp G^{1/5}\), and \(R_{G,\Sigma,0}^{\star}\asymp G^{-4/5}\) under first-order Whitney extrapolation. Disabling that correction gives bias order \(C^{-1}\), cutoff \(G^{1/3}\), and risk \(G^{-2/3}\), the GrahamPowell2012 scalar slow-mover benchmark under \(C=1/h\). Third, if \(K=1\), \(T=5\) near \(x^\star\), then \(Z_k(z)\) has its first positive pole at \(z=2\) with order one for both targets; the selector-distance bound therefore retains \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\asymp G^{-1}\log G\).
statements.justification: These exact reductions test the distance valuation and ensure that the corrected scalar rate is not confused with the uncorrected slow-mover balance.
statements.gap: The finite-support and uncorrected scalar endpoints appear separately in deChaisemartinDHa2025 and GrahamPowell2012, but neither is embedded in a target-specific Hankel phase diagram with distance-weighted correction.
statements.consumer: The reductions give \(\texttt{dist\_lag\_het}\) backward-compatible finite-support behavior and a checkable scalar unit benchmark.

statements.statement: The answer is negative for the frozen class quantified over every nonempty certified signature. There is no universal \(c>0\) for which both \(\operatorname{Risk}_{G,k}(\Sigma)\ge cR_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\) and \(\operatorname{Len}_{G,k}(\Sigma,\eta)\ge c\sqrt{R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}}\) hold for all such classes. A necessary repair is a quantitative interior-slack and coefficient-mean-richness condition permitting two-sided target perturbations while preserving the \(q\)-moment and variance envelopes.

There exists a nonempty certified fixed-signature class with \(T=2\), \(K=0\), and \(S=[2,3]\) for which \(\tau_0(P)=0\) for every member, \(\operatorname{Risk}_{G,0}(\Sigma)=\operatorname{Len}_{G,0}(\Sigma,\eta)=0\), but \(R_{G,\Sigma,0}^{\star}=\sigma^2/(6G)>0\). Thus nonemptiness and the frozen envelope restrictions do not provide the interior coefficient-mean richness needed for a minimax or honest-length lower bound in terms of \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\).

The requested universal matching adaptation factor does not exist under the frozen class. Even with a fixed certified \(\Sigma\), there is no positive constant factor lower bound in units of \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\) or \(\sqrt{R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}}\) that holds over every nonempty class. Moreover, the four resolution indices are deterministic functions of the allowed input \(\Sigma\), so adaptation to them is not a separate statistical experiment within one fixed signature. A positive joint theorem requires a quantitatively rich union of signatures or submodels and a fully specified comparison statistic and critical value.

sampling_model.design: Independent fixed-\(T\) groups under a time-invariant random-coefficient distributed-lag model; \(T\ge2K+2\) is called at least square, while overidentified is reserved for \(T\ge2K+3\).
sampling_model.treatment: A stayer atom at \(X=0\) and a continuous mover density on the one compact semialgebraic support recorded by \(\Sigma\).
sampling_model.overlap: Full column rank holds almost surely among movers because the support has nonempty full-rank interior; all null histories and singular finite-sample events remain defined through Moore--Penrose and fallback conventions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted thresholded projector estimation of \(\Gamma\), fixed-atlas ridge local-polynomial boundary extrapolation, and a finite geometric cutoff grid with an infinity option.

estimand_functional: \(\tau_k=\lim_{C\to\infty}E_P[e_k'M(X)^+(\Delta Y-\Gamma)\mathbf 1\{H_k(X)\le C\}\mid X\ne0]\), with the fixed-signature oracle estimator attaining \(R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4 identifies each eligible mean lag coefficient through a truncated Moore--Penrose score, gives a tuning-free estimator under finite support, and leaves continuous-support cutoff choice delicate.

Theorem 2.1 derives a Gaussian limit at rate \(\sqrt{Gh_G}\) for a determinant-trimmed correlated-random-coefficient estimator, and equation (29) gives an order-\(G^{-1/3}\) mean-squared-error-optimal bandwidth in the scalar positive-density case.
Section 1 gives the height and singular locus of maximal-minor Hankel determinantal rings, and Theorem 2.1 proves rational singularities in characteristic zero.
The Main Theorem upper-bounds the volume of a tube around a real algebraic variety by degree-, codimension-, radius-, and tube-width-dependent polynomial terms.
Theorem 4 stratifies polynomial numerator--denominator pairs into algebraic cells with uniform integral-size formulas, and Theorem 8 converts inverse-integrability into distribution-function bounds.
The paper shows that inverse weights required for point identification can preclude parametric-rate estimation and make rates depend on relative tail behavior.
The Bias Characterization and Asymptotic Distribution Theorems justify derivative-corrected trimming and Gaussian inference for a scalar moment of ratios.
The paper gives consistent estimation and inference with stayers and many scalar slow movers using higher-order bias reduction.
The paper derives between-class expected-length lower bounds and ordered-modulus confidence procedures for linear functionals.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal bias-aware intervals for linear functionals over convex regression classes and uniform asymptotic validity under nonnormal errors.

tldr: Continuous reversible treatment histories identify each heterogeneous lag mean while making its Moore--Penrose score bounded, regular, critical, or irregular. The proposal fixes an original-coordinate geometry signature \(\Sigma\), including a concrete semialgebraic support, the maximal-Hankel-minor ideal, coordinate alignments, active support faces, and a checkable conic normal-link certificate. Real local-zeta integrals define intrinsic target-specific tail and distance-weighted bias indices, including exact logarithmic pole orders, and any normalized subordinate resolution yields the same values. Smoothness is a primitive original-coordinate Whitney condition; a frozen atlas supplies only the partition and implementation. A total cross-fitted estimator uses measurable Euclidean anchor selectors, displayed ridge normal equations, a thresholded projector estimate of the common trend, and a finite whole-class oracle grid. It attains uniform risk and honest-length upper bounds over \(\mathcal P_\Sigma\); construction of a same-signature least-favorable coefficient-mean family is the open step for exact minimax equivalence. The framework preserves target-inactive cancellation, passes the \(K=1,T=5\) exponent-two early-kill test, recovers scalar slow-mover and critical Hankel regimes, and separately recovers the published finite-support root-\(G\) result for \(\texttt{dist\_lag\_het}\).

project_justification.gap: The distributed-lag identification result leaves continuous-history score tails and cutoff choice unresolved. Scalar slow-mover theory cannot see Hankel codimension or coordinate cancellation, while existing algebraic tube results do not provide a fixed-class, boundary-compatible, two-sided probability law with distance-weighted correction.
project_justification.niche: A treatment design supplies a fixed support and repeated anti-diagonal history matrix. Its rank ideal, target alignments, and support faces form a decidable semialgebraic signature whose local geometry can be certified before outcomes are analyzed.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the indices by local-zeta poles, proves their resolution-invariant tail and selector-distance implications, and specifies a total oracle procedure attaining class-level risk and honest-length upper bounds. Same-signature minimax lower bounds and geometry adaptation are exposed as separate open questions with concrete perturbation and selection handles.

related_work: deChaisemartinDHa2025 is the immediate model and consumer: its Theorem 4 supplies the coordinate Moore--Penrose identifying score, while its non-finite-support discussion leaves cutoff choice open. GrahamPowell2012 informs the scalar benchmark through Proposition 1.1, Theorem 2.1, and equation (29); the uncorrected \(G^{-2/3}\) balance is recovered literally, while the distance-weighted first-order correction has \(\zeta_{\Sigma,0,1}=2\) and therefore a different \(G^{-4/5}\) balance. ConcaEtAl2018 informs the nested Hankel rank ideals and singular locus. PhongSturm2000 informs the principalization and local-zeta calculation, and Wongkew1993 and DinhPham2018 provide upper geometric envelopes rather than the proposed two-sided target-specific law. KhanTamer2010 motivates the inverse-weight rate frontier. SasakiUra2022 informs scalar derivative correction, while SasakiUra2026 informs the stayer-plus-slow-mover architecture; neither treats shared Hankel strata. Donoho1994 and CaiLow2004 inform minimax and honest-length moduli, and ArmstrongKolesar2018 informs bias-aware intervals. ArellanoBonhomme2012 anchors fixed-\(T\) random-coefficient identification. GentzkowShapiroSinkinson2011 supplies the reversible newspaper-count application used by \(\texttt{dist\_lag\_het}\).
technical_internal_limitation: The leverage-tail pair alone does not determine post-correction bias. The distance-weighted local-zeta pair is separate, and the selector-distance comparison is therefore an explicit lemma rather than an assumption. The absolutely continuous class \(\mathcal P_\Sigma\) does not contain the separate finite-support comparison law. Exact minimax equivalence is not claimed without a baseline law and same-signature Whitney perturbations jointly realizing both orders. The fixed-signature upper bound also does not imply adaptation across signatures, and coordinatewise shortest intervals do not determine shortest simultaneous-region volume when several lags share an active stratum.
honest_scope: Closed theorem targets are the effective fixed-signature certificate, resolution-invariant local-zeta tail and distance-weighted laws on the finite-exponent branch, eventual zero tails on the bounded-score branch, Borel anchor selection, the selector-distance comparison, total oracle fitting, class-level risk and honest-length upper bounds, and the benchmark reductions. Exact minimax-risk and honest-length lower equivalence remains open until a nonempty baseline and same-signature coefficient-mean perturbations are constructed with all Whitney, moment, variance, and stayer restrictions. The finite-support root-\(G\) statement is an external reduction under the separate discrete law \(P^{\mathrm{fs}}\). Fully data-measurable selection of the dominating geometry and simultaneous lag inference is also open. The \(K=1,T=5\) early-kill statement retains the prespecified alternating history and both target coordinates; the twenty-million-draw uniform-box diagnostic at radius \(0.15\) placed \(u^2P(H_k>u)\) between \(20.10\) and \(20.30\) for \(65\le u\le175\), consistent with the required finite positive limit.
